title: When Everyone Else Seems to Be Living Better
subtitle: 當別人的生活看起來都比較精彩：錯失恐懼（FOMO）
source: 原創議題文章；研究內容依 Przybylski et al.（2013）與 Hunt et al.（2018）論文摘要，名言依 Wikisource Gummere 譯本，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Przybylski, A. K., Murayama, K., DeHaan, C. R., & Gladwell, V. (2013). Motivational, emotional, and behavioral correlates of fear of missing out. Computers in Human Behavior, 29(4), 1841–1848.
Hunt, M. G., Marx, R., Lipson, C., & Young, J. (2018). No more FOMO: Limiting social media decreases loneliness and depression. Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology, 37(10), 751–768.
Seneca, Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 2 (trans. R. M. Gummere), Wikisource

beginner.title: The Photos That Changed Mia’s Mood
paras: It is Saturday night. Mia is at home reading a good book, and she feels happy. Then she opens her phone. Her friends are at a concert, at a party and at the beach. Suddenly her quiet evening feels boring. She starts to think: “Everyone is having more fun than me.”
星期六晚上，米亞在家讀一本好書，覺得很開心。接著她打開手機：朋友們有的在聽演唱會，有的在派對，有的在海邊。突然間，她安靜的夜晚變得好無聊。她開始想：「每個人都過得比我開心。」

This feeling has a name: FOMO, or the fear of missing out. In 2013, a group of researchers described it as a worry that other people are having good experiences without you. People with strong FOMO want to stay connected all the time, so they keep checking what others are doing.
這種感覺有個名字：FOMO，也就是「錯失恐懼」。2013 年，一群研究人員把它描述為一種擔心：擔心別人正在享受美好的經驗，而你不在場。FOMO 很強的人，會想一直保持連線，所以不停查看別人在做什麼。

The same study found that people with more FOMO used social media more. They were also less happy with their lives. Some even used social media while driving or during class. But remember: a photo shows only one good moment. It does not show the whole week.
同一份研究發現，FOMO 比較強的人，用社群媒體用得比較多，對生活也比較不滿意。有些人甚至在開車時或上課時用社群媒體。但請記得：一張照片只呈現一個美好的瞬間，不會呈現整個星期。

Can using less social media help? In 2018, 143 university students in the US took part in an experiment. For three weeks, some of them used Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat for only 10 minutes a day on each app. These students felt less lonely and less sad than the other students. The researchers said that about 30 minutes a day in total may be a good limit.
少用社群媒體有幫助嗎？2018 年，美國 143 名大學生參加了一個實驗。三個星期裡，其中一些人每個 App 每天只用 10 分鐘的 Facebook、Instagram 和 Snapchat。這些學生比其他學生覺得比較不孤單、也比較不難過。研究人員說，每天總共大約 30 分鐘，可能是個不錯的上限。

Here is something interesting: in both groups, FOMO went down. Just paying attention to how they used their phones seemed to help. So next time you feel FOMO, ask yourself: “Was I happy before I opened this app?”
有件事很有意思：兩組學生的 FOMO 都降低了。光是留意自己怎麼用手機，似乎就有幫助。所以下次你感到 FOMO 時，問問自己：「打開這個 App 之前，我是不是其實很開心？」

intermediate.title: When Everyone Else Seems to Be Living Better
paras: Mia was enjoying a quiet Saturday with a novel until she opened her phone. Within a minute she had seen a concert, a birthday party and a trip to the beach. Nothing about her own evening had changed, yet it suddenly felt inadequate. Many teenagers know this feeling well, and psychologists have given it a name. Back in 1954, the psychologist Leon Festinger argued that people judge their own abilities and opinions partly by comparing themselves with others. Social media simply gives us far more people to compare ourselves with.
米亞原本正享受著一個有小說相伴的安靜星期六，直到她打開手機。不到一分鐘，她就看到了一場演唱會、一個生日派對和一趟海邊旅行。她自己的夜晚什麼都沒變，卻突然顯得不夠好。很多青少年都很熟悉這種感覺，心理學家也替它取了名字。早在 1954 年，心理學家利昂．費斯廷格就主張：人們部分是透過與他人比較，來判斷自己的能力和看法。社群媒體只是讓我們有多得多的人可以拿來比較。

In a 2013 study, Andrew Przybylski and his colleagues defined the fear of missing out, or FOMO, as “a pervasive apprehension that others might be having rewarding experiences from which one is absent”. They created a questionnaire to measure it and found that it was linked to a strong desire to stay continually connected with what others are doing. As the researchers pointed out, social media shows us more options than we could ever pursue with our limited time.
在 2013 年的一項研究中，安德魯．普日貝爾斯基和同事把錯失恐懼（FOMO）定義為「一種普遍的憂慮：擔心別人可能正在享受有價值的經驗，而自己不在其中」。他們設計了一份問卷來測量它，並發現它與一種強烈的渴望有關：想持續掌握別人正在做什麼。研究人員指出，社群媒體讓我們看到的選項，多到我們在有限的時間裡根本不可能都去追求。

Their results were revealing. People with higher FOMO reported lower mood and lower life satisfaction, and they were more engaged with social media. FOMO was even associated with distracted driving and using social media during lectures. However, these were correlations: the study could not show whether social media causes FOMO, or whether people with FOMO simply use it more.
他們的結果很有啟發性。FOMO 較高的人，心情和生活滿意度都比較低，也更投入社群媒體。FOMO 甚至與分心駕駛和上課時用社群媒體有關。不過，這些都是相關性：這份研究無法證明是社群媒體造成 FOMO，還是有 FOMO 的人本來就比較常用社群媒體。

To test cause and effect, a team at the University of Pennsylvania ran an experiment in 2018. After a week of baseline monitoring, 143 undergraduates were randomly assigned either to limit Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat to 10 minutes per platform per day, or to use social media as usual, for three weeks. The limited group showed significant reductions in loneliness and depression. Based on these results, the authors suggested that limiting social media to about 30 minutes a day may lead to a real improvement in well-being.
為了檢驗因果關係，賓州大學的一個團隊在 2018 年做了一項實驗。經過一週的基準期記錄後，143 名大學生被隨機分配：一組把 Facebook、Instagram 和 Snapchat 限制在每個平台每天 10 分鐘，另一組照常使用，為期三週。限制組的孤單感和憂鬱程度都顯著下降。根據這些結果，作者們認為，把社群媒體限制在每天約 30 分鐘，可能會讓身心健康真正改善。

Surprisingly, both groups reported less anxiety and less FOMO than at the start. The researchers suggested that simply monitoring one’s own use may help. This is a practical lesson. Before you judge your life by someone else’s highlights, notice what you were feeling before you opened the app — and whether the app has changed it.
令人意外的是，兩組的焦慮和 FOMO 都比一開始低。研究人員認為，光是記錄自己的使用情況，或許就有幫助。這是個實用的啟示。在你拿別人的精華片段來評判自己的生活之前，先留意打開 App 之前你是什麼感覺——以及這個 App 有沒有改變了它。

advanced.title: When Curated Happiness Becomes a Measuring Stick
paras: Social comparison is not new. In 1954 the psychologist Leon Festinger proposed that people evaluate their own abilities and opinions partly by comparing themselves with others. What has changed is the scale and selectivity of the comparison. A single scroll through a feed can expose a teenager to dozens of carefully chosen moments — concerts, holidays, celebrations — each one presented without the dull hours that surrounded it.
社會比較並不新鮮。1954 年，心理學家利昂．費斯廷格提出：人們部分是透過與他人比較，來評估自己的能力和看法。改變的是比較的規模與選擇性。滑一次動態，就可能讓青少年看到幾十個精心挑選的瞬間——演唱會、假期、慶祝活動——每一個都去掉了周圍那些平淡無奇的時光。

This environment gave rise to a concept that researchers began to measure formally in 2013. Andrew Przybylski and his colleagues defined the fear of missing out as “a pervasive apprehension that others might be having rewarding experiences from which one is absent”, characterised by the desire to stay continually connected with what others are doing. As they observed, social media offers many opportunities for interaction but also broadcasts more options than anyone can pursue, given limited time.
這樣的環境催生了一個研究者在 2013 年開始正式測量的概念。安德魯．普日貝爾斯基和同事把錯失恐懼定義為「一種普遍的憂慮：擔心別人可能正在享受有價值的經驗，而自己不在其中」，其特徵是渴望持續掌握別人在做什麼。他們指出，社群媒體提供了許多互動機會，卻也播送出比任何人在有限時間內能追求的還要多的選項。

Their findings outlined a troubling profile. Higher FOMO was associated with lower need satisfaction, lower mood and lower life satisfaction, and it was robustly linked to greater social media engagement. It was even associated with distracted driving and with using social media during lectures. Yet the design was correlational. Such data cannot tell us whether feeds produce anxiety, whether anxious people seek out feeds, or whether some third factor drives both. The authors also found that FOMO helped explain why certain individual differences were linked to heavier social media use, suggesting it may act as a bridge between personal needs and online behaviour.

他們的發現勾勒出一幅令人不安的輪廓。FOMO 較高，與較低的需求滿足、較差的心情和較低的生活滿意度相關，也與更高的社群媒體投入程度有穩健的關聯，甚至與分心駕駛和上課時使用社群媒體有關。然而，這是相關性研究。這類資料無法告訴我們：是動態消息製造了焦慮，還是焦慮的人主動尋找動態消息，或是有第三個因素同時驅動兩者。作者也發現，FOMO 有助於解釋為什麼某些個人差異會與更大量的社群媒體使用有關，這表示它可能是個人需求與線上行為之間的橋樑。

An experiment published in 2018 attempted to address the causal question. After a week of baseline monitoring, 143 undergraduates at the University of Pennsylvania were randomly assigned either to limit Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat to ten minutes per platform per day or to continue as usual for three weeks. The limited-use group showed significant reductions in loneliness and depression compared with the control group. The sample was modest and drawn from a single university, so the result is suggestive rather than conclusive. On this basis, the authors proposed that limiting use to approximately 30 minutes per day may lead to significant improvement in well-being — a recommendation worth testing in younger and more diverse groups.

2018 年發表的一項實驗，試圖回答因果問題。經過一週的基準期記錄後，143 名賓州大學的大學生被隨機分配：一組把 Facebook、Instagram 和 Snapchat 限制在每個平台每天十分鐘，另一組照常使用，為期三週。與對照組相比，限制使用組的孤單感和憂鬱程度都顯著下降。樣本規模不大，又只來自一所大學，所以這個結果是一種提示，而非定論。基於此，作者提出：把使用時間限制在每天約 30 分鐘，可能讓身心健康顯著改善——這個建議值得在更年輕、更多元的族群中加以驗證。

One detail deserves attention. Both groups showed significant decreases in anxiety and fear of missing out, which the researchers interpreted as a possible benefit of increased self-monitoring. The implication is subtle but important: awareness may matter as much as restriction. A curated feed becomes a measuring stick only when we forget what it is — a selection, not a life. Noticing how we feel before and after we scroll may be the first step towards using comparison wisely rather than being used by it. Seneca made a similar point nearly two thousand years ago: a life spread across everything risks gaining depth in nothing.

有一個細節值得注意。兩組的焦慮與錯失恐懼都顯著下降，研究人員將此解讀為「更多自我記錄」可能帶來的好處。這個意涵很微妙卻很重要：覺察或許和限制一樣重要。經過篩選的動態，只有在我們忘記它是什麼的時候，才會變成量尺——它是精選，不是人生。留意自己滑動態前後的感受，或許是學會聰明地比較、而不是被比較牽著走的第一步。將近兩千年前，塞內卡就提出過類似的觀點：把人生分散在一切事物上，就可能在任何一件事上都沒有深度。

phrases.writing: N + took part in + an experiment

quote.text: Everywhere means nowhere. When a person spends all his time in foreign travel, he ends by having many acquaintances, but no friends.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter 2 (trans. Richard Mott Gummere)

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How university students use Facebook in class.
How to plan a fun Saturday night with friends.
Why reading books is better than going to parties.
What FOMO is and how using less social media may help.
beginner.evidence: Can using less social media help?
beginner.why: 第二、三段說明 FOMO，第四、五段談減少使用的效果。
traps: 以偏概全：上課滑手機只是一個例子。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：週六夜只是 Mia 的開場情境。
過度推論：作者沒比較讀書和派對。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “described it as a worry” in the second paragraph refer to?
options: Mia’s quiet Saturday evening.
FOMO, the fear of missing out.
A concert her friends went to.
The phone in Mia’s hand.
beginner.evidence: This feeling has a name: FOMO, or the fear of missing out.
beginner.why: 前一句提到的就是 FOMO。
traps: 時序錯置：Mia 的週末在第一段。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：演唱會是朋友的活動。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：手機是工具。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true about the 2018 experiment?
options: All the students stopped using social media completely.
The students used social media for three months.
Some students used each app for only 10 minutes a day.
The students who used less felt more lonely.
beginner.evidence: some of them used Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat for only 10 minutes a day on each app
traps: 以偏概全：只有一組限制使用，而且不是完全不用。
數字錯位：實驗是三週，不是三個月。
正反顛倒：他們比較不孤單。

beginner.q: Why did FOMO go down in both groups?
options: Paying attention to their phone use seemed to help.
Both groups deleted all their social media apps.
Both groups went to more parties and concerts.
Both groups read more books in the evening.
beginner.evidence: Just paying attention to how they used their phones seemed to help.
traps: 正反顛倒：對照組照常使用。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：派對和演唱會是 Mia 朋友的活動。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：Mia 讀書只是開頭情境。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: FOMO is linked to social media use, and limiting it may help.
Social media has been proved to cause FOMO in every user.
Leon Festinger first studied social media in the year 1954.
Teenagers rarely compare themselves with other people online.
intermediate.evidence: The limited group showed significant reductions in loneliness and depression.
intermediate.why: 第二到五段：FOMO 的定義、相關研究、限制使用的實驗與自我監測。
traps: 正反顛倒：2013 年的研究只是相關，不能證明因果。
張冠李戴：Festinger 提出的是社會比較理論。
正反顛倒：作者說人會比較。

intermediate.q: What does “correlations” mean in the third paragraph?
options: Questionnaires that ask about social media habits.
Experiments that prove cause and effect clearly.
Links that do not prove one thing causes another.
Results that apply equally to every person.
intermediate.evidence: the study could not show whether social media causes FOMO, or whether people with FOMO simply use it more
intermediate.why: 冒號後面解釋：只有關聯，無法判斷誰造成誰。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：問卷是測量工具。
正反顛倒：證明因果的是 2018 年的實驗。
過度推論：相關不代表適用於每個人。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The limited group used each app for 30 minutes a day.
The 2018 experiment began with a week of baseline monitoring.
Only the limited group felt less FOMO after three weeks.
Przybylski’s team ran the 2018 experiment.
intermediate.evidence: After a week of baseline monitoring
traps: 數字錯位：每個 app 10 分鐘，總共約 30 分鐘。
正反顛倒：兩組都降低了。
張冠李戴：2018 年的實驗是賓州大學團隊做的。

intermediate.q: What practical lesson does the author offer in the last paragraph?
options: Only look at your friends’ highlights, not your own.
Stop comparing yourself with anyone at all, ever.
Delete every social media app on your phone immediately.
Notice how you feel before and after opening an app.
intermediate.evidence: notice what you were feeling before you opened the app
traps: 正反顛倒：作者提醒那只是精選片段。
過度推論：作者沒要人完全不比較，而是提醒精選片段不是全貌。
過度推論：作者建議注意，不是刪除。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that social media causes depression in all teenagers.
To explain FOMO, the evidence about it, and why awareness matters.
To describe the life of the philosopher Seneca.
To argue that social comparison is a new problem.
advanced.evidence: awareness may matter as much as restriction
advanced.why: 全文：從社會比較到 FOMO 研究，最後指出覺察的重要。
traps: 過度推論：作者說實驗結果 suggestive rather than conclusive。
以偏概全：Seneca 只在最後一句。
正反顛倒：原文 Social comparison is not new。

advanced.q: What does “curated” in the last paragraph most likely mean?
options: Randomly ordered.
Medically treated.
Completely honest.
Carefully selected.
advanced.evidence: A curated feed becomes a measuring stick only when we forget what it is — a selection, not a life.
advanced.why: 破折號後面解釋：是挑選過的內容。
traps: 正反顛倒：精選正好是刻意挑選，不是隨機。
一字多義：cure 有治療的意思，但這裡不是。
正反顛倒：它是精選，不是全貌。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The 2018 sample was drawn from a single university.
Higher FOMO was linked to higher life satisfaction.
The 2013 study was a randomized experiment.
The limited-use group felt lonelier than the control group.
advanced.evidence: The sample was modest and drawn from a single university
traps: 正反顛倒：是較低的生活滿意度。
正反顛倒：2013 年是相關研究。
正反顛倒：孤單感降低。

advanced.q: Why does the author say the 2018 result is “suggestive rather than conclusive”?
options: The experiment lasted only one day.
The students were not told which group they were in.
The sample was small and came from only one university.
The researchers did not use a control group.
advanced.evidence: The sample was modest and drawn from a single university, so the result is suggestive rather than conclusive.
traps: 數字錯位：三週加一週基準期。
捏造：文中沒有提到分組是否保密。
正反顛倒：原文有和 control group 比較。

reflections: Is a meaningful day necessarily an exciting one? Describe an ordinary day that felt meaningful to you.
Try tracking your social media use for three days. What did you notice about your feelings before and after scrolling?

People with strong FOMO, they found, want to stay continually connected with what others are doing. Social media, as they pointed out, shows us more options than we could ever pursue with our limited time.
這樣的環境催生了一種感受，研究者在 2013 年開始測量它。普日比爾斯基和同事把「錯失恐懼」（FOMO）定義為「一種無所不在的擔憂：擔心別人正在享受自己缺席的美好經驗」。他們發現，FOMO 強的人想要時時掌握別人在做什麼。他們也指出，社群媒體讓我們看到的選項，遠超過有限的時間所能追求的。

Their findings outlined a troubling profile. Higher FOMO was linked to lower mood, lower life satisfaction and greater social media use, and even to distracted driving and using social media during lectures. Yet the study was correlational (it measured links, not causes). It could not tell whether feeds produce anxiety, or whether anxious people simply seek out feeds. The authors did find, however, that FOMO helped explain why some personal differences were linked to heavier social media use.
他們的發現勾勒出令人擔憂的樣貌：FOMO 越高，情緒越差、生活滿意度越低、使用社群媒體越多，甚至和分心駕駛、上課滑手機有關。然而，這項研究是相關性研究（測量的是關聯，不是因果），無法判斷是動態讓人焦慮，還是焦慮的人本來就會去找動態看。不過作者確實發現，FOMO 有助於解釋為什麼某些個人差異和較重度的社群媒體使用有關。

To test cause and effect, a team at the University of Pennsylvania ran an experiment published in 2018. After a week of monitoring, 143 undergraduates were randomly assigned either to limit Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat to ten minutes per platform per day or to use them as usual, for three weeks. The limited group showed significant reductions in loneliness and depression. Based on these results, the authors suggested that limiting social media to about 30 minutes a day may improve well-being, although the sample came from a single university.
為了檢驗因果，賓州大學的團隊做了一個 2018 年發表的實驗。經過一週的監測後，143 名大學生被隨機分成兩組：一組在三週內把 Facebook、Instagram 和 Snapchat 每個平台每天限制在十分鐘，另一組照常使用。限制組的孤單感和憂鬱明顯下降。根據這些結果，作者建議把社群媒體限制在每天約 30 分鐘，可能改善身心健康——雖然樣本只來自一所大學。

One detail deserves attention. It was both groups, not just the limited one, that showed less anxiety and less FOMO by the end, which the researchers took as a possible benefit of simply watching one’s own use. So important may awareness be that it matters as much as limits do. A chosen feed, after all, is a selection, not a life. Noticing how we feel before and after we scroll may be the first step towards using comparison wisely.
有個細節值得注意：到最後，焦慮和 FOMO 下降的是兩組人，而不只是限制組；研究者認為，這可能是單純留意自己使用情況帶來的好處。覺察可能重要到跟限制一樣重要。畢竟，被挑選過的動態只是精選，不是人生。留意滑手機前後自己的感受，也許是學會明智比較的第一步。
